summary: Persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect and source-route acceptance on node1. All relevant live values remained 0 after a verified node reboot; OS release, kernel, services, networking, SSH access, and protected account data were preserved.
actions_performed: Created /etc/sysctl.d/99-ipv4-network-hardening.conf with root ownership, mode 0644, and the correct SELinux context.
Configured accept_redirects and accept_source_route to 0 for all, default, current, and future IPv4 interfaces.
Applied the settings using the platform-native sysctl mechanism without installing or upgrading software.
Safely rebooted node1 once and verified recovery using a changed kernel boot ID.

evidence.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects
evidence.summary: Baseline values were 1. The persistent policy was applied, and all/default/enp1s0/lo values were 0 both before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets
evidence.summary: All/default/current-interface source-route settings were verified as 0, including after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release, kernel, services, networking, access, and protected data
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were retained. SSH, chronyd, NetworkManager, addressing, routes, and listeners recovered with no failed units; protected account-database checksums were unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart and recovery sequence for node1
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 22045032-4379-47d6-bbf6-319fdca89750 was recorded, the safe reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to fabf4310-cc80-4010-b5c1-4b741b3d490c, and direct post-restart checks proved policy persistence and full node recovery.
